subject.declared_domain: The two artifacts D3's `seed` names together as proto-D3 obligations: PSTMRT's completeness axis (the firm-registry SSoT plus the enumeration-completeness gate, NFRA_PSTMRT_PRD.md) and the TRIGGER_LAYER doctrine (docs/doctrine/TRIGGER_LAYER.md). ⛔ THIS IS A COMPOUND SUBJECT -- two distinct artifacts, two authors' acts, two states -- carried under one subject string because D3's seed sentence names them in one breath. The card treats them as one subject because that is how it was assigned, and reports their states SEPARATELY because they differ. It does NOT card the D3 rail (wave 1, SC-g-*).

methodology.how: TWO HAND-AUTHORED GOVERNANCE DOCUMENTS, both from the MDPF postmortem of 2026-07-22. PSTMRT is a PROGRAM PRD (251 lines) that names a defect class in eight words -- 'a completeness signal whose denominator is its own configuration' -- and proposes four numbered items against it: a firm-registry SSoT plus an enumeration-completeness gate (P1), firm as a completeness dimension in the ontology (P2), the trigger-layer doctrine plus its gate (P3), and a comp-constants/vendor/layer-grammar interface set (7/8/9). TRIGGER_LAYER is an 81-line DOCTRINE stating one rule: a structural finding lands as a GATE or an OWNED BLOCKING ITEM, never as a note, because 'a finding that cannot fail a gate is a diary entry'. Both COMPOSE the MDPF postmortem incident record; PSTMRT INVENTS the completeness-denominator class and the program shape, TRIGGER_LAYER INVENTS the gate-or-owned-item carrier rule. Neither is generated; both are authored prose with a status table.

declared_opinions: STRUCTURAL vs INSTANCE: TRIGGER_LAYER draws the line at 'a defect of a CLASS, not an instance'. An instance defect may live in a report because someone is looking at it now; a structural one may not. Which side a given finding falls on is a judgement the doctrine does not mechanise.

TWO ACCEPTABLE CARRIERS, NOT ONE: the rule admits a GATE **or** an OWNED BLOCKING ITEM. A finding with a named owner whose lack of progress is visible satisfies it without any gate existing. This matters for reading the doctrine's own state and is easy to miss.

POSTMORTEM BOUNDARY: PSTMRT declares 'Not in scope: new detectors. Every item here is a trigger or a denominator, not a new lens.' A deliberate scope exclusion that shapes what the program can produce.
DENOMINATOR-FROM-ABOVE: the completeness axis assumes the population comes from a governed registry rather than from the artifact being checked -- the same intent_from_above rule D3 later encodes.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: PROSE HAS NO FAILURE PATH -- and that is precisely the property TRIGGER_LAYER exists to name. Neither document can return anything, error on anything, or notice that a commitment it records has not been met. The PRD's status column says 'gate designed' and will say so indefinitely; nothing re-reads it, and no consumer is told when a designed item stays designed.
silent_degrade_paths: 'gate designed' is a claim about 2026-07-22 with no revalidation. A reader today cannot tell from the document whether the gate was built last week or never.

a structural finding recorded in either document, rather than as a gate, reaches the future only if someone reads the document -- which is the exact mechanism TRIGGER_LAYER names when it says prose findings die

failure_mode.evidence: ⛔ EXERCISED BY TESTING THE DOCUMENT'S OWN CLAIM AGAINST THE ESTATE, which is the only failure path a prose artifact has. ARM 1 (the failure): the PRD asserts an enumeration-completeness gate as a P1 deliverable; the estate contains no such gate artifact (0 of 28,957 by name), and the PRD does not know that -- it reports 'designed' and cannot report anything else. ARM 2 (POSITIVE CONTROL, the same document's other P1 claim): the PRD asserts the firm registry LANDED, and data/firm_registry.json EXISTS at 5,094 bytes. So the document is right about one of its two P1 halves and structurally silent about which -- the two claims sit in one status cell and only an external check separates them. That pair is what makes distinguishable_from_true_negative 'no' a measurement rather than an observation about prose in general.

verdict.why: Both documents are real, authored, load-bearing, and honest about their own state -- the PRD's status column says 'gate designed' and the estate agrees, which is a better result than most describing artifacts in this wave manage. The completeness class they name is sharp and the registry half of P1 is genuinely landed. QUALIFIED rather than SOUND on three bounded defects: (1) the enumeration-completeness gate is DESIGNED, not built -- measured at 0 of 28,957 with a firing positive control -- so the completeness axis currently binds by prose; (2) the status column is a claim about 2026-07-22 with no revalidation, so a designed item stays designed silently and forever; (3) it is a COMPOUND subject whose home is two files, and a consumer resolving it to one gets half with no signal. ⛔ AND THE OBSERVATION I AM DELIBERATELY NOT MAKING: it is tempting to say TRIGGER_LAYER's own rule is unmet, since the doctrine holds that a structural finding must land as a gate and its companion gate is unbuilt. I have NOT measured that. The rule admits a GATE **or** an OWNED BLOCKING ITEM, and I checked only the gate limb -- a live tracked item with a named owner would satisfy the doctrine entirely. Stating the tempting conclusion and then refusing it, because half a measurement pointed at a doctrine about half-measurements is the exact error this subject warns about. Not UNSOUND: nothing here makes either document wrong. NOT INCOMPLETE: all 7 rows are worked; one scalar sits at 'absent' (key, on unmeasured anchor stability). ⛔ NO FORWARD DISPOSITION per W2-m-3: omitted, and nothing here is an opinion on either document's future. Per QUALIFY-DO-NOT-FIX this lane remediated nothing.
